# 1. Introduction 
We are interested in the factors that control the spatial distribution of a given species (habitat and suitability maps) and predict how these will evolve under predicted climate change. Look at the example below from Kraemer et al [2015](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.08347) where the dots represent the observed occurrence of mosquito's in Europe and the color scale represents the suitability (ranging from 1 highly suited to 0 not suitable):
```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
image = "https://iiif.elifesciences.org/lax/08347%2Felife-08347-fig3-v3.tif/full/,1500/0/default.jpg"
cat(paste0('<center><img src="', image,  '"></center>')) 
```

The previous maps are the result of a statistical model where the species presence/absence is modelled as: 
Species Presence/absence ~ Pred1 + Pred2 + … + Predn

We can construct a logistic model if we have a database with observations and predictor variables. Explore the following dataframa
```{r}
load("occurence.Rda")
#head(my_train_df)
```

You can explore this dataset as follows:
```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE) 
#4.a Exploratory analysis 
#summary(my_train_df)
correlation<-cor((my_train_df), use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
library(corrplot)
corrplot(correlation)

#4.b model
myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
summary(myMod)
# #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
#library(MASS)
#dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
library(modEvA)
Dsquared(myMod, adjust = TRUE) #proportion of deviance explained by a GLM
```

If you have spatial data describing the predictors, you could apply the model and create spatial maps. That is what we will do below!

# 2. Objective
The objective of our geoproject is To map the Habitat distribution of a given species, in a given area, In a given temporal moment: current and future climatic conditions. The output should be a change analysis current -> to future (2050 -> 2070 etc)... Something like this
```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
library(geodata)
library(terra) 
library(raster)
library(dplyr)
#setwd("/Users/kvanoost/Downloads/Session 5")
options(geodata_default_path = "/Users/kvanoost/Documents/UCL/Cours/GIS/geodata")
suitability_map_fct<-function(region,genus,species,res,ssp,model){
  ###Description: Function to model the suitability (present and future) of an area for a species.
  ###Inputs:
  ##region of interest (spatVector) should be a country with ISO code , 
  ##genus and species of interset (see https://www.gbif.org/)
  ##res (numeric): resolution 2.5 5 or 10, 
  ##ssp : (character). A valid Shared Socio-economic Pathway code: "126", "245", "370" or "585"., 
  ##model: (character) climatic model for future prediction (see http://worldclim.com/CMIP5v1)
  #The possible CMIP6 models are Climate model abbrevation. One of "ACCESS-CM2", "ACCESS-ESM1-5", "AWI-CM-1-1-MR", "BCC-CSM2-MR", "CanESM5", "CanESM5-CanOE", "CMCC-ESM2", "CNRM-CM6-1", "CNRM-CM6-1-HR", "CNRM-ESM2-1", "EC-Earth3-Veg", "EC-Earth3-Veg-LR", "FIO-ESM-2-0", "GFDL-ESM4", "GISS-E2-1-G", "GISS-E2-1-H", "HadGEM3-GC31-LL", "INM-CM4-8", "INM-CM5-0", "IPSL-CM6A-LR", "MIROC-ES2L", "MIROC6", "MPI-ESM1-2-HR", "MPI-ESM1-2-LR", "MRI-ESM2-0", "UKESM1-0-LL"
  ###Output: 3 suitability maps (or corresponding RasterLayers)
  
  
  ##1. Load sightings data and verification
  
  #1.a Download observations
  sightings <- sp_occurrence(genus=genus,species = species,ext=(region), sp=TRUE, download = TRUE, geo=TRUE)
  sightings <- vect(sightings)
  crs(sightings) <- crs(region)
  
  #1.b Check if there're enough observations of the species in ROI
  if (length(sightings) < 40) stop("Not enough sightings (ie < 40) of this species in the selected region of interest to model the suitability map. Try another species and/or area of study.")
  
  
  ##2. create RasterStack with predictors
  mybio <- worldclim_global(var='bio', res=res,ssp=ssp) #https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html
  mybio_aoi <- mybio %>% crop(region) %>% mask(region)
  
  ##3. Create presence/abscence database
  
  sightings$pres<-1
  
  #3.a Generating random absence points
  set.seed(1975) 
  abs <-  spatSample(region,size=length(sightings),method="random")
  abs$pres=0
  
  #3.b merge the sightings and absence points
  my_occ_df=sightings+abs
  
  #3.c Extract bio variables (from mybio_aio) values for each observation
  my_train_df<-terra::extract(mybio_aoi,my_occ_df,df=TRUE,bind=TRUE)
  my_train_df <- as.data.frame(my_train_df)
  my_train_df <- my_train_df %>% dplyr::select(pres, starts_with("wc")) 
  
  
  ##4. Modelling
  #4.a Exploratory analysis 
  # summary(my_train_df)
  # correlation<-cor(my_train_df, use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
  # library(corrplot)
  # corrplot(correlation)
  
  #4.b model
  myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
  # summary(myMod)
  # #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
  # # library(MASS)
  # # dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
  # library(modEvA)
  # Dsquared(myMod, adjust = TRUE)
  
  
  ##5. Predict habitat occurence

  #5.b Creating suitability layers
  library(leaflet)
  library(dplyr)
  a<-c("1970-2000","2021-2040", "2041-2060",  "2061-2080")
  pal <- colorNumeric(c("#FFFFCC", "#41B6C4","#0C2C84" ), domain = c(0,1),
                      na.color = "transparent")
  ####### Setup loop
  
  years<-c("1970-2000","2021-2040", "2041-2060",  "2061-2080")
  
  my_list <- list() 
  
  for(j in 1:length(years)) {                 # Head of for-loop
    if (years[j]=="1970-2000"){
      raster<-mybio_aoi
    } else {
      #raster<-raster::getData('CMIP5', var='bio', res=res, rcp=rcp, model=model, year= as.numeric(a[j]))
      raster <- cmip6_world(model=model, ssp=ssp, time=years[j], var="bioc", res=res)
      raster<-crop(mask(raster, region),region)
      names(raster)<-names(mybio_aoi)
    }       
    
  
    Pred<-predict(raster,myMod,type='response')   ### Rastermap
    
    map<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
      leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(Pred), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
      leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = raster::values(Pred),
                         title = paste("Suitability",a[j]))
    output<-list(Pred,map)
    my_list[[j]] <- output        # Store output, which is a list, in another list
  }
  ######
  
  #############
  
  #6. Creation outputs
  result <- my_list
  maps<-list(result[[1]][[2]],result[[2]][[2]],result[[3]][[2]],result[[4]][[2]])
  names(maps) <- c('suitabilitymap_2000','suitabilitymap_2030','suitabilitymap_2050','suitabilitymap_2070')
  layers<-list(result[[1]][[1]],result[[2]][[1]],result[[3]][[1]],result[[4]][[1]])
  names(layers) <- c('suitabilityraster_2000','suitabilityraster_2030','suitabilityraster_2050','suitabilityraster_2070')
  
  #6.a Change analysis
  change30<-layers[[2]]-layers[[1]]
  change50<-layers[[3]]-layers[[1]]
  change70<-layers[[4]]-layers[[1]]
  
  pal <- colorNumeric(c("#c45741","#FFFFCC", "#0C2C84" ), domain = c(-1,1),
                      na.color = "transparent")
  map_change30<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
    leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(change30), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
    leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = values(change30),
                       title = paste("Suitability change for 2030"))
  map_change50<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
    leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(change50), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
    leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = values(change50),
                       title = paste("Suitability change for 2050"))
  map_change70<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
    leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(change70), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
    leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = values(change70),
                       title = paste("Suitability change for 2070"))
  maps_change <- list(map_change30,map_change50,map_change70)
  names(maps_change) <- c('changemap_2030','changemap_2050','changemap_2070')
  #7. Return
  #return(list(layers,list(change50,change70,change50_70)))
  results<-(list(maps,maps_change,layers))
  names(results) <- c('suitability_map','change_map','raster_layers')
  return(results)
  #output : a list the 3 predictions and the 3 change rasterlayers or the same as interactive maps
}

region <- gadm(country="MEX", level=0, path='GADM')

output<-suitability_map_fct(region=region,genus = 'ambystoma', species = 'mexicanum',res=10,model="ACCESS-CM2",ssp="126")

library(leafsync)
sync(output$suitability_map)

```

Cool! Now let's break this down and work step by step

# 3. Setting up a workflow

## Summary

A geoproject's workflow can be summarized as follows:

* Identify a clear goal 
* Decompose the framework into small steps: 

    +   the conceptual aspect
    +   the practical aspect : the data I need and the methodology
    +   the coding aspect.
    
As always, consider reproducibility and clear coding ;-)
We can conceptualize the project as follows:
![Concept](Session_4_Picture1.png){width="50%"}

## Define data needs

So what kind of data do we need?

    +   Species occurrences (GBIF)
    +   Species absences: randomly generated
    +   Climatic variables (Worldclim) + Vegetation
    +   A given species
    +   An Area of Interest

Create a gemodel which is able to produce as output a species suitability map (in-class, this will be developped here below). Modify your code in order to get predictions for multiple species and/or future scenarios (challenge).

## Visualize the workflow



![workflow 1](Session_4_Picture2.png){width="50%"}

![workflow 2](Session_4_Picture3.png){width="50%"}

# Coding first steps

At first, let's try to create a code for a specific example, i.e. without any loops and/or function calls. We try to model for a specific species, the axolotl which can be found in Mexico. Note that we can extract the occurences (sightings) of the axolotl using the `sp_occurrence` function of the `geodata` package. This links to the Global Biodiversity data [see here for more info](https://www.gbif.org/). Make sure you understand the options of the `sp_occurrence` function.

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
image = "https://www.axolotl.org/images/animals/axolotl.jpg"
cat(paste0('<center><img src="', image,  '"></center>')) 


```

## 0. Environment

```{r}
#Load libraries
library(geodata)
library(terra) 
library(raster)
library(dplyr)
setwd("/Users/kvanoost/Downloads/Session 5")
options(geodata_default_path = "/Users/kvanoost/Documents/UCL/Cours/GIS/geodata")
```


## 1. Load sightings
```{r}


#Create model for a given region and species:
region <- gadm(country="MEX", level=0, path='GADM')
genus = 'ambystoma'; species = 'mexicanum'

##1. Load sightings data and verification

#1.a Download observations
#library(dismo)
#sightings<-gbif(genus=genus,species = species,ext=sf::st_as_sf(region), sp=TRUE, download = TRUE)
sightings <- sp_occurrence(genus=genus,species = species,ext=(region), sp=TRUE, download = TRUE, geo=TRUE)
sightings <- vect(sightings)
crs(sightings) <- crs(region)
#plot(sightings)

#1.b Check if there're enough observations of the species in ROI
if (length(sightings) < 40) stop("Not enough sightings (ie < 40) of this species in the selected region of interest to model the suitability map. Try another species and/or area of study.")


```


## 2.Load Predictors

Note that we define a resolution, model and scenario for now. We download a long list of potential climatic predictors using the worldclim database, and we use the `bio` variables. See [see here for more info ](https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html)

```{r}
##2. create RasterStack with predictors
res=10;model="ACCESS-CM2";ssp="126"
mybio <- worldclim_global(var='bio', res=res,ssp=ssp) #https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html
mybio_aoi <- mybio %>% crop(region) %>% mask(region)
plot(mybio_aoi)
```

## 3. Occurences
```{r}
##3. Create presence/absence database

sightings$pres<-1

#3.a Generating random absence points
set.seed(1975) 
abs <-  spatSample(region,size=length(sightings),method="random")
abs$pres=0

#3.b merge the sightings and absence points
my_occ_df=sightings+abs
# quickly visualize this
library(leaflet)
leaflet((my_occ_df)) %>% addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    color = ~ifelse(pres == 0,"red", "blue"),
    radius = 1
  )

#3.c Extract bio variables (from mybio_aio) values for each observation
my_train_df<-terra::extract(mybio_aoi,my_occ_df,df=TRUE,bind=TRUE)
my_train_df <- as.data.frame(my_train_df)
my_train_df <- my_train_df %>% dplyr::select(pres, starts_with("wc"))


```

## 4. Logistic Model

```{r}
##4. Modelling
#4.a Exploratory analysis 
# summary(my_train_df)
# correlation<-cor((my_train_df), use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
# library(corrplot)
# corrplot(correlation)

#4.b model
myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
# summary(myMod)
# #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
# # library(MASS)
# # dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
library(modEvA)
Dsquared(myMod, adjust = TRUE) #proportion of deviance explained by a GLM

```

## 5. Apply spatial model
```{r}
#5.b Creating suitability layers
  Pred<-predict(mybio_aoi,myMod,type='response')   ### Rastermap
  
```

## 6. Create a map

And finally, visualize the map
```{r}
#6 Create map
  # you can blank the regions below a treshold
  Pred <- ifel(Pred < 0.01, NA, Pred)
  library(mapview)
  map <- mapview(Pred, col.regions="red", na.color = "transparent",layer.name='Suitability',legend=FALSE) +   mapview(subset(my_occ_df,my_occ_df$pres==1),cex=2,popup=FALSE,layer.name='Observations')
  map
```

# Generalizing the code

Now that it works for one example, we can now create a function which basically is a copy paste of the above, but where we add variables for the parameters. Note the use of a `list` as the output contains the output in spatRaster format, the model performance as well as maps. A list a very usefull when combining different types of data. Note that naming  the list items helps to reference the items more easily aftwards (see below).

```{r}
#### Wrap this in a function
  Presentday_suitability_map_fct<-function(region,genus,species,res){
    ###Description: Function to model the suitability (present and future) of an area for a species.
    ###Inputs:
    ##region of interest (spatVector) could be a country with ISO code , 
    ##genus and species of interset (see https://www.gbif.org/)
    ##res (numeric): resolution 2.5 5 or 10, 
    ###Output: 1 suitability map as a map, a spatRaster suitability map, metric for model performance (Dsquared)
    
    ##1. Load sightings data and verification
    
    #1.a Download observations
    sightings <- sp_occurrence(genus=genus,species = species,ext=(region), sp=TRUE, download = TRUE, geo=TRUE)
    sightings <- vect(sightings)
    crs(sightings) <- crs(region)
    
    #1.b Check if there're enough observations of the species in ROI
    if (length(sightings) < 40) stop("Not enough sightings (ie < 40) of this species in the selected region of interest to model the suitability map. Try another species and/or area of study.")
    
    
    ##2. create RasterStack with predictors
    mybio <- worldclim_global(var='bio', res=res,ssp=ssp) #https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html
    mybio_aoi <- mybio %>% crop(region) %>% mask(region)
    #plot(mybio_aoi)
    
    ##3. Create presence/abscence database
    
    sightings$pres<-1
    
    #3.a Generating random absence points
    set.seed(1975) 
    abs <-  spatSample(region,size=length(sightings),method="random")
    abs$pres=0
    
    #3.b merge the sightings and absence points
    my_occ_df=sightings+abs
    
    #3.c Extract bio variables (from mybio_aio) values for each observation
    my_train_df<-terra::extract(mybio_aoi,my_occ_df,df=TRUE,bind=TRUE)
    my_train_df <- as.data.frame(my_train_df)
    my_train_df <- my_train_df %>% dplyr::select(pres, starts_with("wc"))
    
    ##4. Modelling
    #4.a Exploratory analysis 
    # summary(my_train_df)
    # correlation<-cor(my_train_df, use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
    # library(corrplot)
    # corrplot(correlation)
    
    #4.b model
    myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
    # summary(myMod)
    # #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
    # # library(MASS)
    # # dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
     library(modEvA)
     Dsq <- Dsquared(myMod, adjust = TRUE)
    
    
    #5.b Creating suitability layers
    Pred<-predict(mybio_aoi,myMod,type='response')   ### Rastermap
    
    #6 Create map
   # map <- mapview(Pred, col.regions="red", na.color = "transparent",layer.name='Suitability',legend=FALSE) + mapview(subset(my_occ_df,my_occ_df$pres==1),cex=2,popup=FALSE,layer.name='Observations')
    pal <- colorNumeric(c("#FFFFCC", "#41B6C4","#0C2C84" ), domain = c(0,1),
                        na.color = "transparent")
    map<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
      leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(Pred), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
      leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = raster::values(Pred),
                         title = paste("Suitability"))
    results<-(list(map,Pred, Dsq))
    names(results) <- c('suitability_leafletmap','suitability_raster','Dsq')
    return(results)
    
    
  } 
```

We can now test this function:
```{r}
# test function
  a <- Presentday_suitability_map_fct(gadm(country="MEX", level=0, path='GADM'),genus='ambystoma',species = 'mexicanum',res=10)
```

# Challenge

Building on what we have done there toghether, the challenge is now to further develop this geomodel and to make it broader by also predicting future suitability maps using the cmip climate predictions. Make sure that your model can predict current suitability and suitability for 2030, 2050 and 2070. For example using a loop over the years:

> `years<-c("1970-2000","2021-2040", "2041-2060",  "2061-2080")`

Also make sure your model can handle different models and scenario's.

The output should be a list containing leaflet maps for the current situation, leaflet maps showing the change for each interval relative to the current condition, and the suitability maps for each time interval in spatRaster format. Some tips:

You can store your results as a list, and add them to another list (usual when looping)

> *. `my_list[[j]] <- output        # Store output, which is a list, in another list`
> *. `list(result[[1]][[2]]       # you can acces a list in a list using the double square brackets`

It is good practice to name your items in the list, for example:

> *. `maps_change <- list(map_change30,map_change50,map_change70)`
  `names(maps_change) <- c('changemap_2030','changemap_2050','changemap_2070')`


Have fun!!

library("terra")

##2. create RasterStack with predictors

mybio <- worldclim_global(var='bio', res=res,ssp=ssp) #https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html
mybio_aoi <- mybio %>% crop(region) %>% mask(region)
#plot(mybio_aoi)

##3. Create presence/abscence database

sightings$pres<-1

#3.a Generating random absence points

abs$pres=0

#3.b merge the sightings and absence points
my_occ_df=sightings+abs

#3.c Extract bio variables (from mybio_aio) values for each observation

my_train_df <- as.data.frame(my_train_df)
my_train_df <- my_train_df %>% dplyr::select(pres, starts_with("wc"))

library(leaflet)

#    radius = 1

##4. Modelling
#4.a Exploratory analysis 
# summary(my_train_df)
# correlation<-cor((my_train_df), use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
# library(corrplot)
# corrplot(correlation)

#4.b model
myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
# summary(myMod)
# #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
# # library(MASS)
# # dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
# library(modEvA)

#5.b Creating suitability layers

#6 Create map

  Pred <- ifel(Pred < 0.01, NA, Pred)
  map <- mapview(Pred, col.regions="red", na.color = "transparent",layer.name='Suitability',legend=FALSE) + mapview(subset(my_occ_df,my_occ_df$pres==1),cex=2,popup=FALSE,layer.name='Observations')
 # map
  
  
###################@
  
#### Wrap this in a function
  Presentday_suitability_map_fct<-function(region,genus,species,res){
    ###Description: Function to model the suitability (present and future) of an area for a species.
    ###Inputs:
    ##region of interest (spatVector) could be a country with ISO code , 
    ##genus and species of interset (see https://www.gbif.org/)
    ##res (numeric): resolution 2.5 5 or 10, 
    ###Output: 1 suitability map as a map, a spatRaster suitability map, metric for model performance (Dsquared)
    
    ##1. Load sightings data and verification
    
    #1.a Download observations
    sightings <- sp_occurrence(genus=genus,species = species,ext=(region), sp=TRUE, download = TRUE, geo=TRUE)
    sightings <- vect(sightings)
    crs(sightings) <- crs(region)
    
    #1.b Check if there're enough observations of the species in ROI
    if (length(sightings) < 40) stop("Not enough sightings (ie < 40) of this species in the selected region of interest to model the suitability map. Try another species and/or area of study.")
    
    
    ##2. create RasterStack with predictors
    mybio <- worldclim_global(var='bio', res=res,ssp=ssp) #https://worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html
    mybio_aoi <- mybio %>% crop(region) %>% mask(region)
    plot(mybio_aoi)
    
    ##3. Create presence/abscence database
    
    sightings$pres<-1
    
    #3.a Generating random absence points
    set.seed(1975) 
    abs <-  spatSample(region,size=length(sightings),method="random")
    abs$pres=0
    
    #3.b merge the sightings and absence points
    my_occ_df=sightings+abs
    
    #3.c Extract bio variables (from mybio_aio) values for each observation
    my_train_df<-terra::extract(mybio_aoi,my_occ_df,df=TRUE,bind=TRUE)
    my_train_df <- as.data.frame(my_train_df)
    my_train_df <- my_train_df %>% dplyr::select(pres, starts_with("wc"))
    
    ##4. Modelling
    #4.a Exploratory analysis 
    # summary(my_train_df)
    # correlation<-cor(my_train_df, use="complete.obs") #there are some NA
    # library(corrplot)
    # corrplot(correlation)
    
    #4.b model
    myMod<-glm(pres~ . , data=my_train_df, family = "binomial")
    # summary(myMod)
    # #check the imporance of the variables: dropterm function removes one-by-one one of the variable and test its imporance in the model selection procedure. 
    # # library(MASS)
    # # dropterm(myMod, test = "Chisq")
     library(modEvA)
     Dsq <- Dsquared(myMod, adjust = TRUE)
    
    
    #5.b Creating suitability layers
    Pred<-predict(mybio_aoi,myMod,type='response')   ### Rastermap
    
    #6 Create map
    # you can blank the regions below a treshold
    #Pred <- ifel(Pred < 0.01, NA, Pred)
    #map <- mapview(Pred, col.regions="red", na.color = "transparent",layer.name='Suitability',legend=FALSE) + mapview(subset(my_occ_df,my_occ_df$pres==1),cex=2,popup=FALSE,layer.name='Observations')
    pal <- colorNumeric(c("#FFFFCC", "#41B6C4","#0C2C84" ), domain = c(0,1),
                        na.color = "transparent")
    map<-leaflet::leaflet() %>% leaflet::addTiles() %>%
      leaflet::addRasterImage(raster(Pred), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8) %>%
      leaflet::addLegend(pal = pal, values = raster::values(Pred),
                         title = paste("Suitability"))
    results<-(list(map,Pred, Dsq))
    names(results) <- c('suitability_leafletmap','suitability_raster','Dsq')
    return(results)
    
    
  } 
    
# test function
  a <- Presentday_suitability_map_fct(gadm(country="MEX", level=0, path='GADM'),genus='ambystoma',species = 'mexicanum',res=10)
